Listing metadata vs accessibility engineering vs screenshot design

Accessibility-aware apps blur three workstreams indie teams merge:

  • App Store Connect listing metadata — name, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshot overlay captions on the zh-Hans row. AppLocale scope.
  • UIKit / SwiftUI accessibility APIs — accessibility labels, traits, hints, VoiceOver rotor order, AXTraits configuration. Engineering scope — not AppLocale.
  • Screenshot composition — device frames, Settings → Accessibility hub mockups, re-exporting PNGs with burned-in Accessibility Shortcut headlines. Design scope — AppLocale delivers caption lines you paste or hand to a designer.

This page covers the first bucket for Accessibility hub-centric product pages — the Settings → Accessibility home and multi-feature assistive listing claims, not deep VoiceOver engineering or single-feature Magnifier marketing.

Accessibility hub marketing is not VoiceOver, Magnifier, Live Speech, or Speak Screen

Accessibility-adjacent apps blur several shop guides indie teams conflate. AppLocale covers listing metadata only — hub-level assistive marketing on the product page:

  • Accessibility hub & multi-feature assistive claims (this page) — Settings → Accessibility home, Accessibility Shortcut, Per-App Settings, and hub bullets like AssistiveTouch, Guided Access, Display & Text Size, Reduce Motion, Voice Control, Switch Control, and Spoken Content entry points when your gallery markets several surfaces together.
  • VoiceOver & screen reader (different) — VoiceOver support, Works with VoiceOver, Accessible for VoiceOver, screen reader navigation badges as the lead story. See VoiceOver listing guide — not hub-grid copy.
  • Magnifier & close-up zoom (different) — magnifying glass, reading glass zoom, flashlight magnifier for low vision. See Magnifier listing guide — not Accessibility hub home marketing.
  • Live Speech & type-to-speak (different) — Live Speech, type-to-speak, speak typed text aloud in conversations. See Live Speech listing guide — not hub-grid Spoken Content entry points.
  • Speak Selection, Speak Screen, Typing Feedback & Announce Notifications (different) — selected-text speech, full-page read-aloud playback, spoken keyboard feedback while typing, and Siri notification read-aloud through headphones or CarPlay. See Speak Selection listing guide, Speak Screen listing guide, Typing Feedback listing guide, or Announce Notifications listing guide — not Accessibility Shortcut triple-click marketing.
  • Dynamic Type only (different) — supports Dynamic Type, larger text, scales with system text size as the sole claim. See Dynamic Type listing guide — not full Display & Text Size hub marketing.
  • Reduce Motion only (different) — respects Reduce Motion, fewer animations as the sole claim. See Reduce Motion listing guide — not full Accessibility hub grids.
  • Vehicle Motion Cues only (different) — animated edge dots while riding in a moving vehicle, motion sickness cues, reduce car sickness on iPhone as the sole claim. See Vehicle Motion Cues listing guide — not global animation reduction or full Accessibility hub grids.
  • AssistiveTouch-only (different) — floating home button and virtual AssistiveTouch menu as the lead. See AssistiveTouch listing guide — not multi-feature hub screenshots.
  • Guided Access-only (different) — single-app lock and kiosk mode as the lead. See Guided Access listing guide — not hub-grid marketing.

Your screenshots may show Accessibility icons alongside Focus pickers or Control Center toggles. Listing copy should name the correct surface per frame — an Accessibility Shortcut sheet is not a VoiceOver rotor demo, not a Magnifier zoom frame, and not a Live Speech type-to-speak keyboard unless that is what the frame shows.

Common mistakes on zh-Hans Accessibility hub listings

  • Only localizing title and description — screenshot overlays still say "Accessibility Shortcut" and "AssistiveTouch" on every hub frame
  • Conflating with VoiceOver-only copy — screen reader paragraphs belong on the VoiceOver guide when VoiceOver is the lead, not generic hub-grid marketing
  • Conflating with Magnifier or Live Speech — close-up zoom and type-to-speak badges need their own guides when those are the hero story
  • Machine-translating "Per-App Settings" literally — awkward strings instead of idiomatic 单 App 设置 phrasing Chinese reviewers use
  • Assuming accessibility-aware app = localized storefront — respecting Accessibility in the binary does not auto-fill Connect overlay fields
  • English text burned into PNG exports — Connect caption fields are Chinese but the image file still embeds English Accessibility headlines (a design fix, not a metadata paste)
  • Claiming every hub feature when you support one — zh-Hans copy promises Voice Control and Switch Control when your marketing only shows AssistiveTouch
  • What's New still English after accessibility launch — see What's New in Simplified Chinese when Accessibility support shipped in a recent version
